text:
oliver: Heads-up — onboarding sample app shows duplicated network activity when a coroutine is cancelled mid-request on some Pixel devices. Backend sees two parallel requests for the same endpoint (token refresh), causing a 429 spike.

oliver: Repro: Kotlin coroutine launches Retrofit call via `suspend fun` and user navigates away -> coroutine.cancel() -> UI shows spinner stuck, server logs a duplicate POST for refresh token. Not always reproducible on emulator.

oliver: Minimal snippet:```kotlin
suspend fun fetchProfile(): Profile = withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
  api.getProfile() // Retrofit suspend function
}
// called from viewModelScope.launch { fetchProfile() }
```

katie: I think this is the classic "coroutine cancel doesn't cancel underlying OkHttp call" unless using the CallAdapter that wires cancellation. Which Retrofit version?

oliver: Retrofit 2.9 + okhttp 4.9.3 (SHIPPING sample). Kotlin 1.8.10.

vikram: Yup — suspend functions in Retrofit are implemented by a CallAdapter that should cancel the Call when the coroutine is cancelled, but older retrofit + coroutines versions had a race. If cancellation occurs between enqueue start and adapter wiring, call may continue.

alex-m: Also device-specific because platform thread timing differs. On some devices cancel happens slightly before enqueue finishes and OkHttp still sends out request body.

katie: Quick checks: add an interceptor that logs call.isCanceled() and call.cancel() in onClose, or wrap call in a custom adapter that ties Job to OkHttp Call. Example:```kotlin
val call = service.rawCall(...)
job.invokeOnCompletion { call.cancel() }
```

vikram: Another approach: enable `OkHttpClient.Builder().retryOnConnectionFailure(false)` in the sample to avoid implicit retries duplicating attempts when cancellation races with IO. Also set `callTimeout` to bound long-running sends.

oliver: Tried job.invokeOnCompletion workaround in viewmodel — reduced duplicates but still saw edge-case where backend got two requests with 1-2s gap.

alex-m: If body is streamed (RequestBody that reads from file/inputstream), cancellation during upload can cause the server to have received the full body while the client thinks it cancelled. We should avoid streaming in onboarding sample or use buffered request bodies for small payloads.

katie: For SDK parity: our Java sync + enqueue paths behave differently — Java enqueue ties Call cancellation to thread interruption differently. We should document exact behavior and add test matrix: emulator, Pixel 6/7, API 31/33.

oliver: Filing an issue: reproduce reliably on Pixel 6 API 33 with steps and small repro repo. Will attach network capture and server logs.

ci-bot: CI job queued: https://ci.internal/repro/1747554321-1 - runnable repro + device matrix.

vikram: Longer-term SDK change: add a small Kotlin-specific CallFactory wrapper in our SDK that ensures Job cancellation always calls `call.cancel()` and prevents double-enqueue edgecases by synchronizing adapter handshake. We can expose it as Beta in 1.2.0.

alex-m: For immediate docs: update onboarding guide with: 1) known device-specific cancellation races, 2) recommended temporary mitigation (wrap suspend call with explicit call cancellation handler), 3) avoid streaming RequestBody in sample apps.

oliver: I'll push a patch to the sample app and open a PR to the docs. If we get a reliable repro, we should open an OkHttp/Retrofit upstream ticket.

katie: Thanks — and add a tiny automated integration test that cancels after 5ms in CI against a headless device to catch regressions.

oliver: Done — will follow up with PR links when ready.
